einzeiler: A couple spends three months in Avignon to immerse themselves in French language and…
kurzfassung: Longtime podcast listeners Nan and Marty share their experience of spending three months living in Avignon to improve their French language skills. They discuss renting a home just outside the medieval walls, leasing a car through Peugeot's tourist program, and taking conversation lessons with local teachers. They also offer recommendations for hidden-gem villages, regional cuisine, and practical tips for long-term travel in France.
stichpunkte: Spent three months in Avignon to significantly improve conversational French skills
Rented an apartment just outside the medieval walls and utilized Peugeot's long-term car lease program
Studied with local professional teachers through relaxed conversation sessions rather than formal grammar drills
Explored regional highlights including Vaison-la-Romaine, Arles, Cassis, and quiet hill villages like Séguret
Balanced daily excursions and cooking classes with the traditional rhythm of French life, including midday closures
Offset travel costs by renting out their own home in California during their absence
Emphasized that curiosity and the willingness to speak are far more important than fluency when interacting with locals

clips.hook: Staying for 90 days without a visa
clips.text: The maximum duration for a standard tourist visit without a formal long-stay visa is ninety days.

clips.hook: All-inclusive cost for a three-month car lease
clips.text: A brand-new vehicle lease spanning three months costs two thousand five hundred dollars total with comprehensive zero-deductible insurance included.

clips.hook: Finding a village deader than a doornail
clips.text: A charming hilltop village that bustled with activity during a weekend wedding felt completely deserted when revisited months later.

clips.hook: The clash between American efficiency and French lifestyle
clips.text: American visitors are conditioned to maximize every minute, whereas French daily rhythms force people to slow down and enjoy extended meals.

clips.hook: Dispelling the myth that higher price means better food
clips.text: Americans often mistakenly believe that spending more money guarantees a superior meal, whereas France offers exceptional food at modest prices.

beschreibung:
Annie Sargent chats with Nan and Marty Deniston, two Americans who spent three whole months living in Avignon. They wanted more than a vacation. They wanted real French. Nan started young, studying in Toulouse as a student. Marty didn't start learning until his fifties. Together they hired a private tutor, built their days around lessons and day trips, and leased a car through a program most travelers never hear about. They rented out their own house back home to make the whole trip work. Along the way, they found villages near Avignon that most visitors skip entirely. Press play, get inspired, and hit subscribe so you never miss an episode of Join Us in France.
